title: The Framing Gallery Where Photographs Learn

features.name: the frame that learned to choose its own contents
features.desc-on-touch: An empty wooden frame, magnificent, hanging in the air. You move around it and the landscape visible through it changes—not because the world is moving, but because the frame itself is selecting what it will contain, teaching the eye what matters.

features.name: the wall of photographs that contain each other
features.desc-on-touch: Each image frames the next: a distant hill in one photo becomes the foreground in another; a window in the left photograph opens onto the landscape of the right. They're not copies. They're a conversation about what lies within sight.

features.name: the camera that photographs the person who looks through it
features.desc-on-touch: It sits on a tripod pointing inward. You step in front of it and the lens fills with your own eyes looking back at you, but younger, in a place you've never been, holding something you remember giving away. The corruption is thorough here.

features.name: the dust and light learning to compose
features.desc-on-touch: Motes drift through the terracotta light like they're being arranged by a patient hand. Each speck of dust is a miniature frame, casting its own shadow, composing its own small statement about what can be held and shown.

features.name: the perspective that learned it was being taught
features.desc-on-touch: The gallery's lines all converge at a point you can't quite reach. As you walk toward it, new frames appear further back, and you understand: the whole gallery is teaching you how to see. And now you see: you were being framed all along.

inscription: the gallery teaches the eye what to hold; the eye teaches the gallery what matters
